answer: In this design, each identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result needed to compute the next. GPUs can speed individual operations but cannot parallelize one chain’s dependency; creating clones therefore requires separate chains and added work, not a shortcut around the per-identity delay. Like cedar at a wharf resisting a glacier’s steady force, the time-lock imposes a physical cost, though sufficient hardware can run chains concurrently.
